2. The respondent Nos. 1-3 of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 32 of 1997, in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Golapgonj, Sylhet impleading principal respondents Nos.4 and 5 as principal defendant Nos. 1 and 2, pro-forma respondent Nos. 6 and 7 as pro-forma defendant Nos. 3 and 4, Abdus Sattar, the predecessor of appellants Nos. 1 and 2 as the defendant Nos. 5 and appellants Nos.3-13 as 6-16 Nos. defendants for redemption of mortgage and khas possession in respect of 0.34 acres of land as described in schedule to plaint. Subsequently, it was transferred to the Joint District Judge Third Court, Sylhet and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 51 of 2001. The respondent No. 3 Pulin Ram Malakar died during the pendency of appeal and his legal heirs have been duly substituted. The plaintiff No.1 Gakul Ram Malakar of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997 (re-number as 51 of 2001) died during the pendency of the suit and his legal heir Nikhil Ram Malakar has been duly substituted as plaintiff No. 1(ka). 

 5. The appellant No. 2, the predecessor of appellant No. 1, the predecessor of appellant Nos. 3-6 of Title Appeal No.108 of 2009 as plaintiff Nos. 1-3 instituted Title Suit No.15 of 1994 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Golapgonj, Sylhet impleading the respondents as defendants Nos. 1-22 for declaration of title by adverse possession for more than 12 years of the statutory period, correction of record in respect of first schedule to plaint as shail in place of canel and Khas possession in respect of second Schedule to plaint. Subsequently, it was transferred to the Sub-Judge, Third Court, Sylhet and re-numbered as Title Suit No.52 of 2001. The said Title Appeal No.108 of 2009 was transferred to the High Court Division by Order dated 14-5-2012 passed in Civil Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 2010 and re-numbered as Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014. 

 10. The case of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 in brief, is that the predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants Charan Ram Malakar were owners of the first schedule land as described in schedule to the plaint. Subsequently, the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants became successive owners by inheritance, Gagan Ram and his 2 brothers, predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendant Nos. 9-10 during their life time produced CS Khatian and other documents before the employee of settlement Jarip at the time of preparation of SA Khatian. They believed SA Khatian was prepared in their names. The predecessors of the plaintiffs for their convenience of enjoyment partitioned the suit land along with other lands and accordingly Gagan Ram Malakar got the suit land in his saham. The plaintiffs filled up the suit land with earth. But the defendant Nos. 3-8 evicted the plaintiffs from the suit second schedule land by constructing tin shed building. The plaintiff on several times requested the defendant Nos.3-8 to leave the suit second schedule land in their favour. But the defendants claimed that the land of second schedule was recorded in the name of Government and they took lease from the Government. On searching in the local Tahsil Office, the plaintiffs came to know on 18-2-2014 that the land of first schedule of plaint was recorded in SA Khatian as canal খাল which was incorrect. In fact the suit land should be recorded as সাইলউরা in CS Khatian in the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants. Thus the plaintiffs were cons-trained to file the suit for declaration of title by adverse possession for statutory period of 12 years in respect of first schedule land, decla-ration that SA Khatian is wrong in respect of first schedule land and Khas possession in respect of second schedule land as described in schedule to plaint. 

 20. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate on behalf of defendants Nos.5-16 appellants of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 submits that the root of disputes between the parties based on the deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS and the agreement for reconveyance of the said land executed on the same date stipulated a period of 3 years from the said date that is to say, the time for reconveyance expired on 30th chaitra 1361 corresponding to 24-4-1956 and the said transaction is not attracted by section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. He further submits that a transaction by way of out and out sale with an separate agreement to reconvay deed was not a mortgage before coming into effect of the Presidents Order (PO 88 of 1972) read with Presidents Order 136 of 1972, because of facts such transaction was not a mortgage by definition of "Mortgage" as provided in section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act. He next submits that where the agreement to recovery is embodied in the same document by which sale is effected the transaction is conditional mortgage. He also submits that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to recovery which has been treated to be mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and same was not alive on 3-8-1972, the date of coming into effect of the Presidents Order 88 of 1972. He further submits such transaction is past and closed and the property involved in such transaction will not be redeemable. He finally submits that the trial court erroneously held that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey constituted a complete usufructuary mortgage for 7 years and ignoring the doctrine past and closed decreed the Title Suit No.51 of 2001 for redemption of mortgage and khas of possession in respect of 0.34 acres of suit land is totally illegal. In support of his submissions learned advocate referred the decision reported in 32 DLR(AD) 233, 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90 and 1 BLC (AD) 164. 

 42. Therefore, we find the trial court held the deed in question being No.719 dated 24-4-1952 with an agreement to reconvey being 720 dated 24- 4-1952 constituted a complete usufructuary mortgage for a maximum period of 7 years based on totally misconception of law and facts. So, the decree passed by the trial court for re-deemption of mortgage and khas possession in favour of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 is erroneous. 

 48. Having regard to facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the deed being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 upon which parties are claiming their respective title, the trial court on misconception of law and facts most illegally held the said deed is out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey constituted to be usufructuary mortgage for 7 years and on that basis decreed the Title Suit No. 51 of 2001 for redemption of mortgage and khas possession. Since we have found that heirs of Jahir Ali failed to prove the suit for partition over 0.7 decimals, and 0.2 decimals for declaration of title which is situated in different mouja and unspecified that has no nexus with the present claim, so the trial court rightly dismissed the Title Suit No. 93 of 1994 and Title Suit No. 52 of 2001.
